questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

Sports other then cricket (1)/ should also be given (2)/ their due importance in India (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution: The given sentence talks about sports besides cricket. So, ‘other than’ is the correct phrase for the purpose. ‘Then’ means at that time and is incorrect here. Since the error lies in the first part of the sentence, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

Deeds (1)/ not words (2)/ are what really count. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: The given sentence has no errors at all. The plural subject ‘deeds’ takes the plural verbs ‘are’ and ‘count’. Thus, option 4 is correct.

questions.question:
**The sentence(s) given with blanks are to be filled with an appropriate word(s). Four alternatives are suggested for each question. For each question, choose the correct alternative and click the button corresponding to it.**

Risha ______ a salary of Rs 50,000 every month.
questions.solution: The given sentence states a phenomena that occurs at a regular interval, i.e., Risha receives a particular amount as salary every month. So the sentence is in the simple present tense and must have the following format :** Sub + V1 + s/es + object. **Since Risha is a singular subject, the singular verb ‘earns’ should be used.

questions.question:
**The sentence(s) given with blanks are to be filled with an appropriate word(s). Four alternatives are suggested for each question. For each question, choose the correct alternative and click the button corresponding to it.**

She ______ her mind after seeing the damaged washing machine.
questions.solution: The action mentioned happened in the past, therefore, ‘lost’ should fill the blank space.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which best expresses the meaning of the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Brevity
questions.solution:
The meaning of the given words are as follows:

Brevity => something that is brief; shortness

Crispness => shortness

Fondness => liking

Meekness => mildness, submissiveness

Clearly, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which best expresses the meaning of the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Accord
questions.solution:
The meaning of the given words are as follows:

Accord => give or grant

Confer => grant a title

Dissension => disagreement

Clearly, option 1 expresses the synonym.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which best expresses the meaning of the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Absolute
questions.solution: ‘Absolute’ means ‘complete’. Therefore, option 2 is the synonym.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which is opposite in meaning to the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Swift
questions.solution: ‘Swift’ means rapid or quick. Therefore, slow is the correct antonym.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which is opposite in meaning to the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Fragrance
questions.solution: ‘Fragrance’ refers to a pleasant smell and ‘stench’ is an odor or a bad smell. Therefore, option 2 is the antonym of the given word.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which is opposite in meaning to the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Agony
questions.solution: ‘Agony’ refers to an extreme physical or mental pain. Options 1, 2 and 3 are synonyms. ‘Delight’ means ‘pleasure’ and is the antonym of ‘agony’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/ Phrase.**

Can't judge a book by its cover

options.text: We should not buy books without checking the cover
We should not judge something primarily on its appearance
We should judge something primarily on its appearance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/09efaba1f03f3617f50d67a80057f02c4fe36af7b8b8c30b73666296abfab598.png] The given idiom means **that you cannot decide what something actually is just by judging it from its appearance.** 

***Let's see an example:** The candidate did not look very intelligent, but you **can't judge a book by its cover.***

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/ Phrase.**

To keep body and soul together
questions.solution: The idiom ‘to keep body and soul together’ means to survive in difficult circumstances or manage to live. Thus, option 4 is correct.

questions.question:
**Below are three alternatives which may be used to improve the sentence by replacing the words given in the brackets. You may choose option 1, 2 or 3. In case no improvement is needed, choose 4.**

One must (be working in a job) for which one has a natural talent.
questions.solution:
You don’t work in a job, you *do* it or *take it up*. Therefore, option 3 is the best replacement here.

Option 2 would have been correct had the verb ‘prefer’ been in its base form.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase.**

To verbally express regret for something that one has done
questions.solution:
To verbally express regret for something that one has done wrong means to __***apologize**. *__

Thus, **option 4 is the correct answer.**

questions.solution: The word given in option 4 has been spelt correctly. ‘Disillusionment’ means a feeling of disappointment as a result of realizing that something is not as thought to be.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent sentence.**

Mehak made

P- a terrible mistake

Q- by not going

R- to the party
questions.solution: P should follow the given part as it states what Mehak make. R must follow Q as it states *where* Mehak did not go. Thus, PQR is the correct sequence.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent sentence.**

The next

P- generation should use

Q- the non-renewable energy

R- wisely and sparingly
questions.solution: ‘Generation’ should logically follow ‘next’ to convey an appropriate meaning. Q states what should be used and R completes the sentence by stating how it should be used. Thus, PQR is the correct order in which the given parts should be arranged.

questions.question: Character is that on which the _________ of a nation is built.
questions.solution:
The beginning of the given passage equates ‘character’ with ‘destiny’ ad then goes on to say that something in relation to the nation depends on its ‘character’. Taking a hint from the first sentence, we can say that option 2 is the best fit answer.

Volition => the faculty or power of using one's will

questions.question: One cannot have a great nation with men of _________ character.
questions.solution: As already established ‘character’ plays the role in nation building. Thus, it is the men of small character who **cannot **build a great nation.

questions.question: men and women who look _________ others as the living image of themselves
questions.solution: The phrase to look upon someone means to regard or consider something in a certain way. With respect to the context of the passage, the sentence thus formed would mean that one should consider other s as equal. Thus, ‘upon’ is the best preposition to be used here.

questions.question: whether in public life or student __________,
questions.solution: As the concerned sentence already mentions ‘public life’, ‘life’ fits appropriately after ‘student’ as well.

questions.question: We cannot climb the mountain when the _________ at our feet is crumbling.
questions.solution: What is at your feet is not the heaven, roof or sky but the ground. Thus *ground* is the correct word for the blank space. The phrase thus formed conveys the meaning that it is impossible to achieve big things unless some other important basic aspects are missing.
